previous_bounded_checks.scope: first Git-corruption regression fixtures; fixture PermissionErrors retained below
repaired corruption fixtures before final payload-first error reporting

failures_and_repairs.observation: A coherently rewritten loose Git object and archive passed the first implementation because git cat-file reports the requested object ID without rehashing its bytes.
failures_and_repairs.cause: The first implementation trusted Git object names and ls-tree path output.
failures_and_repairs.repair: Authenticate both pinned commits, every traversed raw tree, and every selected blob with its Git header and bytes before using it.

failures_and_repairs.cause: The initial corruption tests attempted to write a read-only loose object in a disposable test repository. Both raised PermissionError before reaching the verifier.
failures_and_repairs.repair: Make only the disposable fixture object writable and restore its original bytes and permissions in finally.

independent_review.scope: source identity and actual corrupt-object/NUL-name witnesses; not human peer review

limitations: Exact package-source identity is not independent scientific-result verification.
Anonymity, manuscript, licensing, authorship and venue approval remain separate release gates.
Both pinned Git revisions and required objects must be available locally; verification does not fetch them.
The retained ZIP container identity is bound to the exact checked snapshot; supported container formatting differences can preserve payload identity.
